_readme: Weapon families. Each entry here is a GENERATOR over ONE axis: tier. One authored 'Sword' at maxTier 10 becomes 11 real weapons, tier 0 through tier 10. Edit this file, then run Prince's Palace > Build Default Content. TIER IS NOT PLUS. Tier is which sword this is (its attack, its grade, its adjective, its rarity band) and is baked here. Plus is how honed one particular copy is, it rides on the InventoryEntry at runtime, and it scales the FLAT attack only - never the grade, because letting two axes move the same number is how a scaling system stops being readable. See Domain/Stats/ItemUpgrade.cs. REQUIRED per family: id (goes into every generated item id, and item ids live in save files, so never rename it), displayName (the noun in every name), primary (the ONE ability score this family scales on), primaryAtZero and primaryAtMax (grades: S, A, B, C, D, E, or none). Optional: description, maxTier (default 10), slot (default Weapon), attackAtZero / attackAtMax (default 3 and 18, interpolated between and floored - this is the FLAT half of a weapon's power), secondary / secondaryAtZero / secondaryAtMax (a second scaling stat, same two-ended curve as primary), alsoScalesWith (flat '<score> <grade>' lines that do not move with tier), spellScalesWith (flat '<score> <grade>' lines for what this weapon contributes to SPELL power - deliberately not tiered, see ItemDefinition.spellScaling), requiresAtZero / requiresAtMax (what a character needs before this weapon counts as worn, interpolated the same two-ended way), cost and costPerTier (default 0 and 0; weapons are loot, not Store stock, and FullRunTests asserts it), sortOrder, iconSheet and iconLevels (per-level art from tools/slice_item_sheet.py), tierAdjectives (one word per tier, lowest first; the last one covers everything past the end of a short list). GRADE IS ANCHORED AT BOTH ENDS and interpolated, exactly like a set piece's stats: 'C at tier 0, S at tier 10' is two words rather than eleven letters that drift, retuning is editing the two you have an opinion about, and raising maxTier stretches the curve instead of running out of ladder. A grade may not go DOWN as tier rises - a better sword must never scale worse, and that is rejected rather than generated. Names come out as '<tier adjective> <family>': 'Keen Sword', with any plus appended at display time. Ten is the neutral ability score; every point above multiplies damage and every point below divides it - see ScalingProfile and Assets/_Project/Scripts/Domain/Stats/ScalingGrade.cs for what each grade is worth per point. ITEM-MODIFIER PLAN PHASE B: the old per-family modifier axis (sturdy/nimble/hallowed/arcane/verdant/heavy/quick/cunning) is gone - a base weapon now carries one default scaling identity (Sword->STR, Staff->INT, Dagger->DEX), and rolled Rift modifiers are what differentiate one drop from another now (modifiers.json), not the weapon family itself.

families.description: A length of something that grew, carrying something that did not.
Short, light, and quick to the point. A first real weapon, and a last resort.
